title: Affine K-projective Hom-complex representatives
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring, with specified derived categories of $A$-modules and of module sheaves on $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pc-derived-category]. Let $M$ be an arbitrary integer cochain complex of $A$-modules, and let $T$ be termwise associated sheaf (the functor koszulOpenTilde of [def-sc-koszul-open-system]). A complex $L$ is K-projective if every chain map from $L$ into an acyclic complex is null-homotopic. There are additive equivalences $a_{L,h_L}:\operatorname{Hom}(Q(TL),Q(TM))\simeq H^0(\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_A(L,M))$ for all K-projective $L$ and proofs $h_L$ of K-projectivity, where the module Hom complex is [def-sc-module-total-hom-complex]. For K-projective $L,L'$, a chain map $g:L'\to L$, and any Hom-complex chain map $t$ with $t^n(z)=\operatorname{ofHom}(g)\circ z$ in every degree, $a_{L',h_{L'}}(Q(Tg)\circ\phi)=H^0(t)(a_{L,h_L}(\phi))$. Moreover, for every $\phi:Q(TL)\to Q(TM)$ there are a chain map $g:L\to M$ and a cycle $z\in Z^0(\operatorname{Hom}^{\bullet}_A(L,M))$ such that $Q(Tg)=\phi$, the inclusion of $z$ into degree-zero cochains is $\operatorname{ofHom}(g)$, and $a_{L,h_L}(\phi)=\pi(z)$ for the canonical homology projection.

proof.text: Use exists_affineQCohDerivedEquivalence_core to obtain a fully faithful additive functor F from the module derived category into the sheaf derived category, together with η: Q ⋙ F ≅ T ⋙ Q. Its additivity follows from the supplied triangulated structure. Full faithfulness follows from the equivalence and full-subcategory inclusion.

For K-projective L use Mathlib IsKProjective.Qh_map_bijective to turn Qh.mapAddHom into an additive equivalence. Conjugate by quotientCompQhIso, then apply the fully faithful F.mapAddHom equivalence and conjugate by η. This gives c from homotopy morphisms to affine sheaf derived morphisms. Naturality of the two comparison isomorphisms proves c(H.map f)=Q(T.map f).

Compose c.symm with moduleHomComplex_quotient to define a. Surjectivity of the homotopy quotient gives a chain map f representing c.symm φ; the quotient lemma provides its cycle z and projection identity. This proves all representative identities.

To prove naturality, represent φ by f and z. Apply the quotient lemma to g ≫ f to obtain z′. The cycles inclusion is injective; cyclesMap_i, the given formula for t, and Cochain.ofHom_comp prove cyclesMap t z=z′. The representative formulas for a and homologyπ_naturality then give the desired equality.

theorem affineKProjective_homComplex (A : Type u) [CommRing A]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w}
      (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings (Spec (.of A)).toRingedSpace))]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{v} (ModuleCat.{u} A)]
    (M : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) :
    let T := (koszulOpenTilde A).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    ∃ a : ∀ (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (_hL : L.IsKProjective),
        (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj L) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj M)) ≃+
          (CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex L M).homology 0,
      (∀ (L L' : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ)
        (hL : L.IsKProjective) (hL' : L'.IsKProjective) (g : L' ⟶ L)
        (t : CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex L M ⟶ CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex L' M),
        (∀ (n : ℤ) (z : CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cochain L M n),
          (t.f n) z = (CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cochain.ofHom g).comp z (zero_add n)) →
        ∀ φ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj L) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj M),
          a L' hL' (DerivedCategory.Q.map (T.map g) ≫ φ) =
            HomologicalComplex.homologyMap t 0 (a L hL φ)) ∧
      ∀ (L : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} A) ℤ) (hL : L.IsKProjective)
        (φ : DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj L) ⟶ DerivedCategory.Q.obj (T.obj M)),
        ∃ (g : L ⟶ M) (z : (CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex L M).cycles 0),
          DerivedCategory.Q.map (T.map g) = φ ∧
          (CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex L M).iCycles 0 z =
            CochainComplex.HomComplex.Cochain.ofHom g ∧
          a L hL φ = (CochainComplex.moduleHomComplex L M).homologyπ 0 z
